RISCO VuPoint · working reference · 23 November 2026

Camera & NVR settings

A searchable companion to Remote Configuration: what each control is for, how related controls interact, and where the supplied manuals explain it.

Scope and evidence

This reference combines the open QA site’s remote-configuration interface with the uploaded IP Camera User Manual (5IN3148) and NVR User Manual (5IN3149). Page numbers are PDF page numbers.

Inspected deviceFirmwareCoverage
RVNVR324K1RA · 32-channel NVRVC1.3.0-261118Main menus; connected-camera controls, including 8MP fixed and 5MP varifocal channels; newer integration/recognition pages.
RVCM92A370RA · thermal cameraVC47.55.1.3.6-261116Main menus, optical analytics, thermal image controls, fire detection and temperature measurement.
RVCM61W360RA · 4MP PT Wi-Fi cameraVC39.24.1.3.10-261117Menu differences, display/image, wireless and general system pages. PTZ operation/settings are supplemented by the NVR manual.

Coverage limit: this is a broad reference for the observed firmware and manual families, not a guarantee that every VuPoint model exposes every option. The 4/16-channel NVRs were not independently re-enumerated for this document. Disabled event pages, empty integration tables, hardware-dependent dialogs, and options revealed only by changing a mode can hide additional fields. No Save, output trigger, reboot, format, reset, or firmware operation was executed. Inspection exception: opening Add under thermal Temperature Measurement → Area created a disabled row (ID 1) that remained after reload. The initial area list was empty. Cleanup was blocked by automatic approval review and requires user approval; the temperature detector remains disabled.

Evidence labels: Manual wording reproduces the supplied manual’s explanation. Explanation is a plain-language interpretation of an observed label and its configuration context; an attached manual link supports the corresponding concept, not necessarily every sentence or this exact firmware. Needs confirmation marks an unresolved control. A menu being visible is not proof that its function is implemented by the selected camera.

How the settings fit together

Input / detector
What triggers?→Rule + active schedule
Where, when, which targets?→Alarm linkage
Record, beep, output, email…→Destination settings
Duration, output schedule, server…
  • Video quality ≠ recording schedule. Main/sub/third stream settings control encoding; Record enables storage; the schedule selects when/reasons; event linkage selects the affected channels.
  • Input ≠ output. Normally Open/Closed describes how an input sensor is interpreted. An event output has its own latch duration and schedule. Manual Trigger operates the output immediately; it does not configure the detector.
  • Buzzer ≠ camera siren. The NVR buzzer, a camera speaker, visible deterrence and electrical alarm output are separate actions.
  • Thermal ≠ optical analytics. The observed thermal camera lists CH1 as “Thermal main” and CH2 as “Camera”, but CH2 exposes the thermal palette/measurement controls. Identify the channel by its capabilities, not the editable name. Optical Fire & Smoke Detection and thermal Fire Detection are different functions.
  • Cloud connectivity ≠ event push. RISCO Cloud connection, RISCO Cloud Push, third-party event push and email have separate configuration paths.
  • Local settings ≠ device settings. Download/snapshot paths and browser playback preferences affect the client computer, not camera encoding or NVR storage.

Thermal measurement notes

The generic manuals do not document the thermal calibration fields. The explanations here are interpretations of the observed thermometry controls. Emissivity, reflected temperature and distance are measurement compensation inputs; a palette is visual presentation. Neither a color change nor a displayed temperature is proof that an alarm rule is configured. Measurement accuracy, supported ranges, alarm conditions, and suitability for a particular application require the model’s thermal specifications or confirmation from RISCO.

Temperature-area rows expose Enable, Name, Rules, Emissivity, Distance, Reflective Temperature and Setup. A disabled inspection-created row showed Point as its rule type; further geometries and alarm-threshold fields were not verified. Fire/temperature schedule and alarm-linkage tabs were visible. Empty or asynchronously loading panes were not used to infer hidden controls.

Finding a setting

Search a label such as ANR, Latch Time, emissivity, or a menu such as IEEE802. “Observed UI” lists page inventories. “Manual library” adds family-level settings and conditional options absent from the current page. Open a result to read the explanations and page links. The page works offline; keep the source PDFs beside index.html when uploading this folder to GitHub Pages.

Additional model comparison: 5MP and 8MP

Direct camera comparison, 23 November 2026. Menu visibility is distinguished from verified behavior. This pass used navigation only; no Add, Save or detector-enable action was used.

ModelFirmwareInspection coverage

RVCM52A350RA		VC31.35.1.3.6-261114Direct camera remote configuration: display, expanded image, recording/main/sub/audio, capture, privacy mask, event panes, plate-management availability, network, platform, system and maintenance menus. Disabled controls and configuration-changing operations were not exercised.
8MP fixed bullet
RVCM52A510RA		VC49.57.1.3.11-261105Direct camera remote configuration: display, expanded image, recording/main/sub/third/audio, capture, privacy mask, event inventory/linkage and network menus. The remaining system, platform, maintenance, storage, alarm, statistics, cloud/email/security, user and information menus were captured after access was renewed. Fall Detection, multi-target, flame/smoke and license-plate Settings panes were inspected.

RVCM32A330RA		VC31.35.1.3.6-261114Direct remote configuration inspected after access renewal: expanded image, recording/main/sub/audio, capture/mask, event settings, license-plate availability, storage, deterrence/siren, network/platform, system, users, maintenance and information pages. Newly inventoried settings and model differences

Setting / modelPurpose or differenceEvidence and limits
Fall Detection
8MP fixed bullet		Analytic intended to identify a person falling. Its settings page was inspected on the 8MP fixed bullet: Long Distance Mode, Loitering Duration(s) (0–10), target-size limits, sensitivity, Bounding Box, Result Box and Detection Area. Accuracy, dependencies and alarm behavior were not tested. This purpose is inferred from the label.Detailed Settings page inspected. Not present in the captured 5MP bullet or dome event menus; no detector was enabled or tested.
Result Box
8MP fixed bullet		An additional analytic result-display overlay switch observed on the 8MP camera. It is separate from Bounding Box. The supplied manuals do not establish its exact visual contents or whether it is embedded in every output stream; behavior was not tested.Observed under Event Settings; separate switch from Bounding Box. Exact effect needs confirmation.
Long Distance Mode
8MP fixed bullet		A Fall Detection mode intended for more distant subjects, inferred from its label. The 8MP exposes it as a switch; the exact detection-distance range and algorithm change are not explained by the supplied manuals and were not tested.Observed in the Fall Detection Settings pane after maintenance access renewal; not toggled.
Face Database Management
8MP fixed bullet		Manages reference faces for recognition, distinct from face detection/capture. The 8MP exposes this additional List Management tab. The current page reports unavailable in the current state; database fields and recognition behavior were not exercised.Observed tab and unavailable-state message. The 5MP dome and bullet expose only License Plate Management in this menu.
Dome versus varifocal bullet
5MP dome and 5MP varifocal bullet		The inspected dome exposes the same common image controls (including Corridor Mode), two encoded video streams, input/output audio volumes, Deterrence, Siren and plate-related controls as the inspected 5MP bullet. No additional dome-only setting label was established in this navigation pass.Direct comparison of RVCM32A330RA and RVCM52A350RA, both VC31.35.1.3.6-261114. Physical optics and hidden mode-dependent controls were not exercised.
Corridor Mode
5MP varifocal and 8MP fixed bullets		Rotates the image for narrow vertical scenes such as corridors. It is separate from horizontal/vertical flip and angle adjustment. The camera manual describes a 90-degree clockwise corridor mode (p. 34).Observed switch in expanded Image Settings on both models; already described in the manual library, newly inventoried for these cameras.
Loitering Duration(s)
5MP varifocal bullet		Minimum time an eligible target must remain in an intrusion region before the dwell/loitering condition triggers. The observed 5MP Intrusion page uses seconds.Observed in Intrusion settings. The concept already exists in the manual library; the firmware-specific label was added.
Mainstream / Substream / Thirdstream
5MP versus 8MP bullets		The inspected 5MP menu exposes Mainstream and Substream; the 8MP also exposes Thirdstream. Each stream has separate encoding settings. Do not apply a three-stream assumption to the 5MP model.Observed Video Parameters tabs. Stream profile limits and permitted resolutions/codecs were not exhaustively enumerated.
Illumination controls
5MP versus 8MP bullets		The 5MP exposes Image Setting/Smart Illumination and White Light controls plus Deterrence and Siren menus. The 8MP image page exposes IR-CUT Mode, IR-CUT Sensitivity, IR LED Control and Low Beam Light; its captured main menu has no Deterrence or Siren page.Observed menu/control difference at the current configuration. Mode-dependent alternatives were not revealed by changing settings.
Audio controls
5MP versus 8MP bullets		The 5MP Audio page exposes Output Volume, Input Volume and Audio Encoding. The 8MP Audio page exposes Input Volume, Audio Encoding and Sampling Rate; Output Volume was absent from that pane.Observed controls; absence from this pane is not an independently verified hardware specification.
License Plate / List Management
5MP varifocal bullet; 8MP menu inventory		Plate detection/capture and list-based recognition are separate functions. The 5MP detection page exposes Select Mode, Snap Mode, Snapshot Interval, plate-type target, Detection Mode, LPD Enhance and Capture Vehicle Image. Its License Plate Management page reports that the feature is unavailable in the current state.Settings panes inspected on both bullets and dome. The 8MP adds Face Database Management; its face/plate management pages and the 5MP plate-management pages report unavailable in the current state. No detector was enabled to expose hidden options.
Multi-Target-Type Recognition / Fire & Smoke Detection
8MP fixed bullet		These analytic entries are visible on the inspected 8MP firmware. The captured 5MP bullet menu does not list them. Multi-target analytics and optical flame/smoke detection are separate from thermal thermometry.Settings panes captured on 8MP after access renewal. Resource compatibility and event behavior were not tested.
Physical I/O menu availability
5MP varifocal and 8MP fixed bullets		Neither captured direct-camera main menu exposes I/O or Combined Alarm. Do not carry over the thermal camera I/O controls to these cameras, or infer that an NVR alarm input is a camera terminal.Observed menu absence on these models/firmware; confirm physical hardware support from each model specification.

The interrupted comparison resumed after maintenance access was renewed. The remaining 8MP menus and the 5MP dome were inspected. Conditional options requiring mode changes, disabled database editors, and actual event/output behavior remain untested; Result Box and Long Distance Mode effects require confirmation. No settings were saved, detectors enabled, or Add controls used during this comparison.

8MP Fixed Bullet CameraEvent Settings Fall Detection Settings8 controls

Analytic intended to identify a person falling. Its settings page was inspected on the 8MP fixed bullet: Long Distance Mode, Loitering Duration(s) (0–10), target-size limits, sensitivity, Bounding Box, Result Box and Detection Area. Accuracy, dependencies and alarm behavior were not tested. This purpose is inferred from the label.

SettingPurpose / effectEvidence

5MP Varifocal Bullet CameraModel comparison and additional event-menu entries8 findings
SettingPurpose / differenceEvidence / limits
Dome versus varifocal bulletThe inspected dome exposes the same common image controls (including Corridor Mode), two encoded video streams, input/output audio volumes, Deterrence, Siren and plate-related controls as the inspected 5MP bullet. No additional dome-only setting label was established in this navigation pass.Direct comparison of RVCM32A330RA and RVCM52A350RA, both VC31.35.1.3.6-261114. Physical optics and hidden mode-dependent controls were not exercised.
Corridor ModeRotates the image for narrow vertical scenes such as corridors. It is separate from horizontal/vertical flip and angle adjustment. The camera manual describes a 90-degree clockwise corridor mode (p. 34).Observed switch in expanded Image Settings on both models; already described in the manual library, newly inventoried for these cameras.
Loitering Duration(s)Minimum time an eligible target must remain in an intrusion region before the dwell/loitering condition triggers. The observed 5MP Intrusion page uses seconds.Observed in Intrusion settings. The concept already exists in the manual library; the firmware-specific label was added.
Mainstream / Substream / ThirdstreamThe inspected 5MP menu exposes Mainstream and Substream; the 8MP also exposes Thirdstream. Each stream has separate encoding settings. Do not apply a three-stream assumption to the 5MP model.Observed Video Parameters tabs. Stream profile limits and permitted resolutions/codecs were not exhaustively enumerated.
Illumination controlsThe 5MP exposes Image Setting/Smart Illumination and White Light controls plus Deterrence and Siren menus. The 8MP image page exposes IR-CUT Mode, IR-CUT Sensitivity, IR LED Control and Low Beam Light; its captured main menu has no Deterrence or Siren page.Observed menu/control difference at the current configuration. Mode-dependent alternatives were not revealed by changing settings.
Audio controlsThe 5MP Audio page exposes Output Volume, Input Volume and Audio Encoding. The 8MP Audio page exposes Input Volume, Audio Encoding and Sampling Rate; Output Volume was absent from that pane.Observed controls; absence from this pane is not an independently verified hardware specification.
License Plate / List ManagementPlate detection/capture and list-based recognition are separate functions. The 5MP detection page exposes Select Mode, Snap Mode, Snapshot Interval, plate-type target, Detection Mode, LPD Enhance and Capture Vehicle Image. Its License Plate Management page reports that the feature is unavailable in the current state.Settings panes inspected on both bullets and dome. The 8MP adds Face Database Management; its face/plate management pages and the 5MP plate-management pages report unavailable in the current state. No detector was enabled to expose hidden options.
Physical I/O menu availabilityNeither captured direct-camera main menu exposes I/O or Combined Alarm. Do not carry over the thermal camera I/O controls to these cameras, or infer that an NVR alarm input is a camera terminal.Observed menu absence on these models/firmware; confirm physical hardware support from each model specification.
8MP Fixed Bullet CameraModel comparison and additional event-menu entries11 findings
SettingPurpose / differenceEvidence / limits
Fall DetectionAnalytic intended to identify a person falling. Its settings page was inspected on the 8MP fixed bullet: Long Distance Mode, Loitering Duration(s) (0–10), target-size limits, sensitivity, Bounding Box, Result Box and Detection Area. Accuracy, dependencies and alarm behavior were not tested. This purpose is inferred from the label.Detailed Settings page inspected. Not present in the captured 5MP bullet or dome event menus; no detector was enabled or tested.
Result BoxAn additional analytic result-display overlay switch observed on the 8MP camera. It is separate from Bounding Box. The supplied manuals do not establish its exact visual contents or whether it is embedded in every output stream; behavior was not tested.Observed under Event Settings; separate switch from Bounding Box. Exact effect needs confirmation.
Long Distance ModeA Fall Detection mode intended for more distant subjects, inferred from its label. The 8MP exposes it as a switch; the exact detection-distance range and algorithm change are not explained by the supplied manuals and were not tested.Observed in the Fall Detection Settings pane after maintenance access renewal; not toggled.
Face Database ManagementManages reference faces for recognition, distinct from face detection/capture. The 8MP exposes this additional List Management tab. The current page reports unavailable in the current state; database fields and recognition behavior were not exercised.Observed tab and unavailable-state message. The 5MP dome and bullet expose only License Plate Management in this menu.

Mode-dependent alternatives were not revealed by changing settings.
Audio controlsThe 5MP Audio page exposes Output Volume, Input Volume and Audio Encoding. The 8MP Audio page exposes Input Volume, Audio Encoding and Sampling Rate; Output Volume was absent from that pane.Observed controls; absence from this pane is not an independently verified hardware specification.
License Plate / List ManagementPlate detection/capture and list-based recognition are separate functions. The 5MP detection page exposes Select Mode, Snap Mode, Snapshot Interval, plate-type target, Detection Mode, LPD Enhance and Capture Vehicle Image. Its License Plate Management page reports that the feature is unavailable in the current state.Settings panes inspected on both bullets and dome. The 8MP adds Face Database Management; its face/plate management pages and the 5MP plate-management pages report unavailable in the current state. No detector was enabled to expose hidden options.
Multi-Target-Type Recognition / Fire & Smoke DetectionThese analytic entries are visible on the inspected 8MP firmware. The captured 5MP bullet menu does not list them. Multi-target analytics and optical flame/smoke detection are separate from thermal thermometry.Settings panes captured on 8MP after access renewal. Do not carry over the thermal camera I/O controls to these cameras, or infer that an NVR alarm input is a camera terminal.Observed menu absence on these models/firmware; confirm physical hardware support from each model specification.

Setting / optionManual explanationSource

Auto/GPIO Autoauto control switching mode, color switching black and white by image judgement, black and white conversion color by photosensitive judgement.Camera manual p. 34

OFFNo light is used for fill.Camera manual p. 34

DisableNo exposure compensation optimisation is performed on the picture frame.Camera manual p. 35

Automatic modeAdjust the white light using default parametersCamera manual p. 35
ManualActively set the synthetic gained white light of red, green, and blue.Camera manual p. 35
ShutterSet the length of shutter exposure. (Some models have support for aperture setting; those that do not have support for aperture setting have only automatic and manual modes)Camera manual p. 35
Automatic modeThe program automatically selects an appropriate exposure time and aperture value according to the currently set Time Exposure and Iris range.Camera manual p. 35
ManualDirectly uses the currently set Time Exposure time and Iris aperture value.Camera manual p. 35
Shutter FirstShutter First is the aperture value obtained by metering the camera with a manually defined shutter.Camera manual p. 35
Iris FirstAperture priority, where the size of the aperture is defined manually and the camera's metering is used to obtain the corresponding shutter value.Camera manual p. 35
Exposure TimeSet the exposure time of the camera, used in combination with Shutter. When the exposure time is long, the image will be overblown, and when the exposure time is short, the image will be dark.Camera manual p. 35
Defog ModeDefog mode. Turn it on to make the picture clearer in rainy and foggy weather. 3D Noise Reduction: Reduces noise in the image to make the picture clearer,Camera manual p. 35
Automatic modeThe camera automatically selects the noise reduction effect according to the algorithm.Camera manual p. 36
OFFNoise cancellation is not switched on.Camera manual p. 36
ManualNoise reduction is performed according to the manually set noise reduction coefficient.Camera manual p. 36

Setting / optionManual explanationSource
Record SwitchSelect to enable recording in this channel.NVR manual p. 40

Setting / optionManual explanationSource
ResolutionDetermine the record to main stream type. Higher values offer greater detail. The default resolution is auto-selected by your NVR.NVR manual p. 41
Frame RateSet the frame number of the main stream.NVR manual p. 41
Encoding FormatList the supported codec for the connected camera. H.265 compresses. information more efficiently for better video quality at a given bandwidth. H.265+ offers even greater compression. H.264 requires higher bandwidth and offers less efficient compression. H.264+ provides additional compression compared to H.264. Please note that only some devices support H.264+ and H.265+. Please note that in the substream, some cameras also support the MJPEG format. If you choose this encoding format, during preview, only one channel of MJPEG encoding will be displayed.NVR manual p. 41
Encoding ModeFor simple scenarios, such as gray wall, a constant bit rate (CBR). For more complex scenarios, such as busy streets, a variable bit rate (VBR) is appropriate.NVR manual p. 41
Video QualityAvailable only for VBR, this setting allows to select the recording quality, here are several options like Lowest,Lower,Low,Medium,Higher,Highest.NVR manual p. 41
Config ModeSelect either User-defined mode to manually set the bitrate or Predefined mode to choose from predefined bitrate.NVR manual p. 41
BitrateDetermines the speed of data transfer used for video recording. Higher bitrates result in better-quality recordings but require more bandwidth. Adjust incrementally until satisfied with image quality.NVR manual p. 41
AudioEnables or disables audio recording if your camera supports it. Make sure to enable Audio streaming in the Audio Encoding section if you want to record audio.NVR manual p. 41
I Frame IntervalThis parameter sets the interval between I frames (keyframes) in the IP camera's stream. I frames are full frames, while other frames are encoded based on the differences from preceding frames (P frames or B frames). A shorter interval can improve video quality but may increase bandwidth usage.NVR manual p. 41
ETRETR (Event Trigger Recording) allows to adjust codec stream parameters for recording based on whether an alarm is present or not. This optimization ensures that crucial events, such as motion detection or alarm activation, are captured with optimal quality and efficiency.NVR manual p. 41

Min. Focus DistanceWhen the distance between the scene object and the lens is less than the minimum focus distance, the lens will not change the focus on that object and will prioritize focusing on objects at distances greater than the "Minimum Focus Distance" parameter. For example, if the minimum focus distance is set to 6 meters, you can set a baffle at 1.5 meters to block part of the lens's field of view, with one half showing a distant view and the other a close view. Setting / optionManual explanationSource
Format HDDSelect the hard disk that needs to be formatted, click Format HDD button, and perform the formatting operation after checking the password from the pop-up menu.NVR manual p. 57
NAS HDDSupport the configuration of network hard disk for recording and capture storage. You need to create a storage partition on the network hard disk in advance and successfully connect the network hard disk on the device through the network. (Note: AI database, license plate database and video prompts file only is stored in local HDD drive.）NVR manual p. 57
Mounting TypeChoose the mounting type from NFS and SMB/CIFS. You would need to input the account name and password of NAS if you choose SMB/CIFS.NVR manual p. 57
OverwriteThis instructs your NVR to overwrite the oldest video files as the hard drive becomes full. You also have the option of selecting the amount of days for recordings to be kept before they are overwritten. For example, if you choose the option 7 days then only the last 7 days' recordings are kept on the HDD. To prevent overwriting any old recordings, select OFF. If you have set Off on this feature, please check the HDD status regularly to make sure the HDD is not full. Recording will be stopped if HDD is full. We recommended leaving the Auto selection as this prevents your NVR from running out of storage space.NVR manual p. 58
Record on ESATAThis menu only displayed when your NVR is coming with an E-SATA port on the rear panel and your E-SATA HDD has been connected to the NVR already. It will allow to record the video to external E-SATA HDD to enhance your HDD capacity. If the E-SATA recording function is enabled, E-SATA backup function will be disabled. If your NVR supports to install multiple hard disks and more than 1 hard disk is installed in your NVR, the edit button will be appear in your system, you can click it to edit the HDD as below picture.NVR manual p. 58
Disk TypeYou can set the hard disk to be Read Write, Read Only, or Redundant. ⚫ Read Write type is the normal status for an HDD to save recordings or search recordings to play. If all the installed hard disks are set to Read Write mode, the NVR will save recordings to the hard disks sequentially. ⚫ To prevent important video data from being overwritten during cyclic recording, the hard drive disk can be set as Read Only type. New recordings will not be able to be saved to this read-only disk. You can still search and play recordings from this read-only disk. ⚫ A Redundant hard disk can be used to save the same recordings as what is saved to the Read Write hard disk(s). When a redundant disk is set, the system can save recordings in parallel to both the Read Write hard disk and the redundant hard disk in case of hard disk failure.NVR manual p. 58
Disk GroupYou can set the disks into different disk group for recording.NVR manual p. 58

SensitivitySet detection sensitivity level from 1-100. The larger the value, the easier it is to trigger.NVR manual p. 74

Bounding BoxWhen enabled, a green bounding box will be displayed on the images, outlining and identifying detected targets. This aids in quickly locating and recognizing captured objects of interest.NVR manual p. 74

There are two modes available, please choose according to your specific needs. ⚫ Hybrid Mode: In this mode, both static and moving targets are detected. It combines detection of both stationary objects and those in motion. Hybrid mode is beneficial in scenarios where both static and moving objects may be of interest for surveillance. ⚫ Motion Mode: This mode exclusively detects moving targets within the frame. It focuses solely on identifying objects in motion, ignoring stationary elements.NVR manual p. 74
Trigger ModeUsed to set the area and path for triggering target detection, it allows you to customize the area or path that triggers detection, enabling the system to focus on the specific areas and movement paths you are concerned about.NVR manual p. 75
RectangleIn this mode, you can draw a rectangular area as the detection area. Any targets entering this area will be detected and trigger the corresponding alarms or actions.NVR manual p. 75

Rule TypeUnder the Line mode, you need to draw a line inside the preview area, and set the crossing direction Rule Type (A->B or B->A) so that when a face crosses the line according to the set rule, it will be detected and trigger a response - suitable for scenarios requiring monitoring of targets crossing a certain path or boundary line.NVR manual p. 75
